techniques.name: Cold Calling
techniques.description: A strategy where the teacher calls on students to answer questions regardless of whether they have raised their hands. It keeps all students engaged and accountable.
tasks: Plan questions to ask throughout the lesson.
Ensure you call on different students to promote active participation.
Use cold calling to check for understanding.

techniques.name: Socratic Questioning
techniques.description: A method of questioning that encourages critical thinking and deep understanding. It involves asking a series of thought-provoking questions that lead students to examine their assumptions and reasoning.
tasks: Encourage students to think critically about the material.
Guide students to deeper understanding through inquiry.

techniques.name: Think-Pair-Share
techniques.description: A collaborative learning strategy where students think about a question individually, then discuss their thoughts with a partner, and finally share their ideas with the larger group.
tasks: Incorporate think-pair-share activities to encourage peer interaction.
Allow students to articulate their thinking.
Facilitate class discussions based on pair-sharing.

techniques.name: Effective Questioning Techniques
techniques.description: Using a variety of questioning techniques to promote engagement, assess understanding, and stimulate higher-order thinking. This includes open-ended questions, probing questions, and wait time.
tasks: Plan a mix of question types to use throughout the lesson.
Give students time to think before answering.
Use follow-up questions to deepen understanding.

techniques.name: Feedback Loops
techniques.description: The process of providing students with timely, specific feedback on their performance and using that information to guide future learning. It involves cycles of feedback and response.
tasks: Provide regular, constructive feedback on student work.
Use feedback to adjust instruction and support learning.
